title: Plain parallel Pollard rho on secp256k1 (no negation map or GLV classes) with a deterministic round meter

claims.statement: For the uniform full-production secp256k1 target Q=[x]P, the classical cold attack in proof.md (plain R=2048-adding parallel Pollard rho with distinguished points, no negation map or order-6 classes, start-replay recovery, and a round/event meter) halts on every run after at most W_max < 2^128.9844 target-group-operation equivalents: each walk step is one protected reference operation (batched incomplete affine addition, 6M, A=0) plus the per-batch inversion share and control charged in instructions under C=1000; all other work is charged through itemised analytic instruction allowances (M=512, A=64, I=2^19). It succeeds with probability at least 0.39 under the disclosed random-mapping heuristic H1 with a factor-2 margin (kappa=2) in the birthday constant. Peak memory < 2^99 bytes; preprocessing < 2^36.2 units, included; every random-sampling loop is capped (halt with failure) so the bound covers every execution; no nonuniform advice. The submitted rational bound is justified by the exact inequality W_max^100 <= 2^12900 checked in experiment.py. Not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Production curve checks and exact rational ledger/score inequality; end-to-end toy runs of the specified algorithm on small prime-order a=0 curves measuring success, wrong outputs and the empirical birthday constant kappa.
